subtype: Approach: reviewing feedback and adjusting the timeline [Revision]
passage: In the district bank's small IT office, Rashmi said quietly, "Ajay, your technical work is strong, but I haven't yet seen leadership." Ajay had hoped this would be his cycle. He walked to the tea stall across the road and drank slowly, watching the bus stand. "If leadership is what they want to see, one cycle isn't enough to show it," he told himself. Back at his desk he wrote a new plan: mentor the new intern, Prabha, from the first of next month, and lead the demo for the regional heads in March. He would aim for the next cycle instead. He showed the plan to Rashmi, who asked him to review it with her every month.

qa.q: Who did Ajay plan to mentor?
qa.a: Ajay planned to mentor the new intern, Prabha.

qa.q: How did Ajay feel when Rashmi said leadership had not yet been seen?
qa.a: Ajay felt disappointed, having hoped it would be his cycle, and needed time alone at the tea stall to take it in.

qa.q: What else could Ajay do to show leadership, and why?
qa.a: Ajay could take on organising the team's weekly planning, because guiding others in a small everyday task also counts as leadership.

qa.q: How might the intern Prabha benefit from Ajay's plan?
qa.a: Prabha would probably feel supported and learn faster, with a mentor who has time set aside for the role.

grounding: Illustrates hearing that leadership is not yet shown, letting go of the current cycle and planning to mentor an intern and lead a demo for the next one.
